transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you too, Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. 

Um, well, I guess I'm here because... well, I've been having a little bit of trouble keeping track of things lately. I'm sure it's nothing too terrible—probably just normal aging, you know? I really don't want to make a big fuss out of it. 

But, my family thought I should come in because I keep forgetting things I really shouldn’t. Important things, like, uh, my heart follow-up appointments, or I'll completely forget to call the clinic back when I'm supposed to. And even just little things, like if I'm doing a repair job around the house, I'll show up to do it and realize I didn't bring the right tools with me. 

It’s a bit embarrassing to admit, honestly, taking up your time with it. But... does that make sense? I hope I'm in the right place for this kind of thing, Doctor.
Over what period of time have you noticed these memory lapses becoming more frequent?

Oh, um, let me think. I really don't want to make it sound like a bigger deal than it is, I promise. But I suppose it’s been causing real trouble for... maybe about a year and two months? Give or take. 

It sort of started after I had a bit of a cardiac scare. I'm okay now, really, I don't want you to worry! But it did force me to cut back on all the walking and the little hands-on projects I used to do around the house. Those things always used to keep me, you know, settled down and on track. Without them, I guess I've just been a lot more scattered. 

Does that timeline help at all, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Aside from the memory lapses, have you been feeling significantly sad, hopeless, or have you lost interest in the activities you used to enjoy over this past year?

Oh, goodness, no. No, nothing like that, thank goodness. I really don't want you to think I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself, or anything like that. 

I mean, sure, I get a little frustrated with myself when I mess up and forget a call, but I'm actually a pretty upbeat guy! I definitely haven't lost interest in things. Even if I can't do the heavy physical work or the long walks anymore, I still like keeping busy however I can, you know? Tinkering with smaller things, or just enjoying the day. 

I always try my best to keep a positive attitude so I'm not a downer for my family. I hope that's a good sign? Am I answering your questions alright, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.
When these memory lapses occur, would you say they have been gradually worsening over time, or did they seem to appear suddenly after that cardiac event and have stayed about the same since then?

Oh, gosh, that’s a really good question, Dr. Smith. I... I’m actually not entirely sure, to be honest. I feel a little silly not knowing, since it’s my own brain, but I really haven't kept very close track of it. I'd hate to give you the wrong answer and mess up your notes. 

I suppose... well, I really only started noticing it being a nuisance after the heart thing, when I had to stop moving around so much. But as for whether it's getting worse or just staying about the same... I really couldn't say for sure. It just sort of feels like it's... there? 

I'm so sorry, I know a doctor prefers exact answers and that's probably not very helpful at all. Is it okay if I'm not totally sure about that one? I can try to think on it a bit harder if you need me to!
Have you noticed any new physical symptoms since that cardiac event, such as weakness in your limbs, difficulty with your balance, or any changes in your speech?

Oh, no, no, nothing like that at all. Honestly, physically, I feel pretty darn good! I definitely don't have any weakness or trouble talking, or anything scary like that. 

I mean, I know I'm getting up there in years, and I had that little scare, but I don't want you to think I'm falling apart! My balance is just fine, and I can still get around the house without any trouble. I just have to take it a little easier than I used to, that's all. 

I really hope that's what you were hoping to hear? I'd hate for you to think there's something else wrong with me when I'm actually doing pretty well, physically speaking. Does that sound okay to you, Doctor?
When you are working on your small projects or tasks at home, do you find that you have more difficulty planning out the steps or organizing how to get the job done than you did a few years ago?

Oh, planning things out? No, I wouldn't say I have any trouble with that. I mean, I'm just tinkering around with little things anyway, so it's not like I'm trying to build a whole house or anything complicated! 

I just sort of... jump right in and figure it out as I go. I've always been a bit of a do-er rather than a planner, you know? I like to just get my hands on things and see what happens. I really don't think I've lost a step when it comes to figuring out how to fix a hinge or sort out a little project. 

I try to keep things pretty simple so I don't make a mess of things for my wife. I hope that makes sense? I just want to reassure you that I'm still very capable of handling my little chores around the house. I'm doing alright on that front, wouldn't you say?
Have you ever been told by a doctor that you have had a stroke or a mini-stroke?

Oh, goodness, no. No doctor has ever said anything like that to me. A stroke? No, definitely not. 

I mean, the heart thing was scary enough, but my brain is... well, it's perfectly fine in that regard! I’ve never had any mini-strokes or anything that would cause alarm like that. I’ve always tried to take decent care of myself, you know, and I’ve been very lucky to avoid anything that serious with my head. 

I hope you weren't worried that I might have had one without knowing? I promise I would have told you right away if a doctor had ever mentioned something like a stroke. I'm doing my best to be a good patient and give you all the right information, I really am! That's a good thing, right? No strokes on my record!
Do you find that there are some days when your memory and thinking feel much clearer than on other days?

Well, you know, I think... I think I'm pretty steady, day to day. I don't really have these big swings where I'm sharp one day and completely foggy the next. 

I mean, sure, if I haven't slept well, maybe I'm a little slower to get going, but that's just normal for a guy my age, right? It's nothing drastic. I definitely don't want you thinking my mind is playing tricks on me or going in and out. I feel like I'm pretty consistent up here. 

I really try to stay on top of things, and I feel like my thinking is usually just fine. I hope that's the kind of answer you're looking for? I'm doing my best to be honest, and honestly, I think my head is on pretty straight most days! That sounds normal, doesn't it?
Have you ever experienced periods where you seem unusually drowsy or have been seen staring blankly into space for long periods, even when you aren't tired?

Oh, drowsy? Staring blankly? No, no, I wouldn't say that at all. I mean, maybe if I'm watching a boring television program I might nod off for a second, but who doesn't do that, right? 

I certainly don't just sit around staring at the wall when I'm wide awake. I've got too much energy for that! I'm always tapping my foot or fiddling with something. My wife says I'm like a wind-up toy sometimes. So no, no blank staring or anything concerning like that. 

I want to make sure you know I'm staying active and alert. I wouldn't want you to think I'm just wasting away in a recliner all day! That's not me at all. I'm still full of pep, wouldn't you agree? I hope that puts your mind at ease about that sort of thing.
Have you ever seen things, like people or animals, that you know aren't actually there?

Oh, goodness, no. No, definitely not. I mean, my eyesight isn't quite what it used to be—I need my reading glasses for the paper these days—but I certainly don't see things that aren't actually there! No imaginary people or animals or anything strange like that. 

I'm very grounded in reality, I promise you. I'd tell you if I did, honestly, but my mind doesn't play tricks on me. I'm perfectly sound in that department! That's exactly what you want to hear, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job answering these for you. Everything sounds okay so far, right?
Have you ever been told by a doctor that you have high blood pressure?

Oh, high blood pressure? No, no doctor has ever mentioned that to me. I've always been told my blood pressure is right where it should be. 

I mean, I try to take good care of myself, you know? I stay active, keep moving... probably too much moving sometimes, to be honest! But my heart and everything, it's all ticking along just fine. I always make sure to ask when I go in for my checkups, and they always say I'm doing great. 

I definitely don't want you worrying about my physical health on top of everything else. I'm keeping myself in pretty good shape for a guy my age! That's a good thing, right? I hope that's helpful for your notes.
Could you try to recall three common objects that I might tell you, such as a pen, a watch, and a chair, after we talk for a few more minutes?

Oh, absolutely! I can definitely do that for you. A pen, a watch, and a chair. See? I've got them locked in already! 

I'd be more than happy to remember those for you. My memory is still sharp as a tack, I promise. I know I can be a little, well, fidgety while we sit here—like I said, always tapping my foot—but I'm really paying close attention to everything you're saying. I'll just keep those three things tucked away in my head while we talk. 

Pen, watch, chair. I'm doing okay so far, right? Just let me know when you want me to repeat them back to you later, and I'll be ready!
Could you please tell me those three objects I asked you to remember a few minutes ago?

Oh, the objects! Yes, of course. Let's see... a pen, a watch, and... oh, goodness. A pen, a watch... and... 

Well, isn't that silly of me? I had it right on the tip of my tongue, I swear I did! I was just so focused on answering all your other questions perfectly, you know? I wanted to make sure I gave you all the right details. 

It was a pen, a watch, and... oh, I'm drawing a complete blank on the last one. I'm so sorry! I usually have a wonderful memory, I really do. I just get a little, well, wound up sometimes when I'm trying to be helpful. I hope I didn't mess up your test too badly! I'm still doing alright overall, aren't I? I can try again if you want!
When you have these memory lapses, do you find that you have difficulty finding the right words to use during a conversation?

Oh, no, no, nothing like that. I don't have any trouble finding words at all. I mean, we're having a lovely conversation right now, aren't we? I think I'm keeping up my end of things just fine! 

I'm definitely not one of those people who just sits there staring blankly, trying to think of what to say. If anything, I probably talk a little too much! I've always got plenty of words ready to go. I just got a little distracted with that memory thing, that's all. It's not a regular problem, I promise. My mind is still working perfectly well for a conversation. I'm making sense, right? I hope I'm giving you all the right answers.

Have you noticed any instances where you've had trouble following the steps of a familiar task or keeping up with a conversation in a group setting compared to how you handled those situations a few years ago?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I have trouble with anything like that. I mean, I've been doing the same things around the house for years, and I still get them all done! Everything gets finished just fine. 

And as for group conversations, well, I love talking with people! I'm always right in the middle of it. Sometimes I might, you know, jump in a little quick or talk over someone by accident because I get so excited about the topic, but I'm definitely keeping up. I don't feel lost or anything. I'm still just as sharp as I was a few years ago. I'm giving you the right kind of information, aren't I? I just want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you need.
Are you still able to manage your own finances, such as paying your monthly bills or balancing your checkbook, without any help from your family?

Oh, absolutely! Yes, I handle all of that myself. No problem at all. I mean, my wife sometimes... well, she likes to organize the mail when it comes in, but I'm the one who actually sits down and writes the checks. 

I've always been very responsible with our money, you know? Sometimes I might, um, maybe rush through it a little bit because sitting still with a checkbook isn't exactly the most thrilling way to spend an afternoon, but everything gets paid! I haven't needed anyone to take over for me or anything like that. I'm still perfectly capable. That's a good sign, isn't it? I hope that shows I'm still doing well.

Have you noticed that you have become more prone to making small, uncharacteristic errors when handling your finances, such as miscalculating a total or forgetting to pay a bill on time, even if you are still managing them yourself?

Oh, well... no, not really. I mean, I certainly wouldn't say I make uncharacteristic errors. Like I said, I rush a bit sometimes because sitting there with the bills is just so tedious, you know? I just want to get it done and move on to something else. 

So maybe, once in a great while, I might transpose a number or, you know, a bill might get buried under a magazine on the counter for an extra day or two before I put it in the mail. But that's just because I'm moving fast, not because I'm making real mistakes. Everything always gets sorted out right away. I'm definitely not losing my touch or anything like that. That's completely normal, right? Everyone misplaces a piece of mail now and then when they're busy. I'm still doing a good job with it all, don't you think?
Has anyone close to you, such as your wife, ever expressed concerns that your memory lapses are causing you to struggle with daily tasks that you used to perform easily?

Well, my wife... she does worry a little bit sometimes. But I think she just fusses over me because she cares, you know? It's not that I'm really struggling with daily tasks or anything major like that. 

I suppose... well, the reason I'm actually here today is because I have been forgetting a few little things lately that I probably shouldn't. Just silly things, really! Like, um, I might forget to call the clinic back, or I'll miss a follow-up appointment for my heart. And sometimes I'll start a repair job around the house—I'm always fixing things, I love staying busy—but I'll show up to fix the sink and realize I didn't bring the right tools with me from the garage. 

But it's just because I've got so much on my mind and I'm always on the go, right? It's not a serious problem. I just get a little ahead of myself sometimes. That's a pretty common thing to happen at my age, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the whole picture so you can tell me I'm doing okay.

Aside from the small errors you mentioned, has your wife or family had to step in to help you with things like grocery shopping, cooking, or managing your medications because they were worried you might make a mistake?

Oh, no, no. Nothing like that! I mean, my wife does the grocery shopping, but that's just because she always has, you know? She likes to pick out the produce herself. And cooking... well, I've never been much of a chef, so she handles that too. But it's certainly not because they're worried I'd mess it up! 

As for my pills, I take them myself. I mean, sure, she bought me one of those little plastic boxes with the days of the week on it, but that's just to keep things neat. I pop them out every morning while I'm having my coffee. I'm perfectly capable of handling all that. I haven't needed anyone to take over my chores or look after me like a child. I'm still doing my part around the house, keeping busy. That's exactly how it should be, right? I'm doing fine on my own.
